title: Dev Dock Manager (Rust)
subtitle: Development Environment Manager (Rust)
description: One Docker dev box per user, with a web terminal, a noVNC desktop and optional GPU. The Django version, rewritten in Rust, partly to find out whether I could.
longDescription: A high-performance development environment management system built with Rust and Docker. This platform provides isolated, containerized development environments for multiple users on the same machine, featuring a Rust-based backend API with JWT authentication, WebSocket support for real-time console access, and a React/Next.js frontend. All services run behind Traefik reverse proxy with optional Nvidia Docker support.
solutions: Built WebSocket handlers for real-time console
Used Bollard for Docker API integration
Created JWT-based auth system with SQLite + Argon2
why: The Django manager needed Django, Daphne and an RQ worker under supervisord, and idled at 175 MiB doing nothing. The Rust version is one binary that idles at 5.5 MiB and starts about six times faster, which leaves more of the machine for the desktops it hands out.
gains: The pick for new setups: the same dashboard, routes and permissions as the Django version, so users can't tell which one they got, while the backend image shrinks from 687 MB to 144 MB and there's one binary to babysit instead of Daphne plus an RQ worker.

flow.label: Log in, keep a JWT pair

lessons: The rewrite answers most calls 4 to 6 times faster, but the two list calls mostly wait for Docker, so there the gap is only 1.2 to 1.6 times.
Log-in time is mostly password hashing (Argon2 here, PBKDF2 in Django), so not all of that speed-up belongs to the language.
/health lives on the API inside the Docker network. Traefik doesn't route it, so localhost:8000/health from the host gets the frontend's 404.
